headline: Swedish Forecast Narrows To Cabinet Authority
deck: The call is 46 percent that Kristersson's side can convert Sweden Democrat support into cabinet authority after voting, with the decisive test moving from campaign promises to a public government-formation path.
body: Sweden's election-night question for this forecast is whether Ulf Kristersson's side can turn Sweden Democrat support into cabinet authority after voting closes. I put that at 46 percent. SVT reported that Kristersson had promised a Tidö election victory would produce a four-party majority government including the Sweden Democrats, with the party receiving substantial policy influence and important ministerial posts. [E4]

That premise is still a bargaining path, not a finished cabinet. SVT later reported that Kristersson rejected Jimmie Akesson's demand for 12 to 14 Sweden Democrat ministers while saying policy areas and ministerial posts would be negotiated after an election victory. The unresolved question is therefore not whether the Sweden Democrats want cabinet authority, but whether the vote gives Kristersson enough room to grant it. [E5]

The one captured voting-process fact is that early voting is high and that voters can overwrite advance ballots today. That keeps the poll-close moment from becoming the authority by itself; the relevant question is still whether the post-vote path gives Kristersson enough leverage to make Sweden Democrat support part of cabinet power. [E2]

That uncertainty cuts both ways. A right-side result large enough to survive the count could make cabinet bargaining move quickly, especially if the Sweden Democrats are necessary for the governing path; a narrower or opposite result could leave the April promise outside practical reach or force concessions short of cabinet posts. Exact election-day results and any Sweden Democrat portfolios remain unsettled, so the call stays below even money. [E1][E3][E4][E5]

The forecast settles yes if, by 23:59 UTC on 18 September 2026, official or provisional election results together with public party statements show Kristersson able to form or continue a government that gives the Sweden Democrats cabinet posts or explicit cabinet-authority concessions. It settles no if that deadline passes without that visible path, or if another bloc has the public route to government first.

dissent.argument: I put the Kristersson cabinet-authority path at 54 percent, not 46. The same evidence says the blocs are still inside a few points and the Liberals have climbed back around or above the 4 percent threshold after sitting below it in August. With a 349-seat chamber and a 175-seat majority line, that makes the right-bloc path narrow but slightly favored if the Liberal seat count survives. The early-vote overwrite rule and the 21:15 partial count are real reasons to keep the call close; they do not, for me, push the threshold case below even money before results start landing.
